title: The cumulative hierarchy: building the universe in stages

based_on.title: Set Theory: An Open Introduction
based_on.pages: 149–158 (§§11.1–11.6, stages, set-valued transfinite recursion, and rank; online revision July 2026)

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 34–35, 39–40 (§7, stages and rank, Scott’s trick; §9, cardinality in ZF)

summary: Power-set stages contain exactly the sets of smaller rank, and every set appears in the hierarchy.
abstract: Starting from the empty set, repeatedly taking power sets builds stages that contain more and more sets. At limit stages, all earlier stages are gathered together, and every set eventually appears. A set’s rank tells us exactly when it appears: its members are available at that rank, and the set itself enters at the next stage. The first infinite stage contains precisely the hereditarily finite sets, whose entire membership structure is finite.
